blocks.x: Where most programs improvise, ai security & model protection as we deliver it is sequenced: Secure the models themselves — prompt-injection defense, agent containment and AI red-teaming. The sequence matters more than the stack — both are documented here.
What we deliver under this name

AI systems add a new class of vulnerability: prompt injection through retrieved content, data poisoning in training pipelines, model theft via extraction, and agents that can be talked into harmful tool use. We deliver AI-specific security architecture — input/output filtering, retrieval content sandboxing, tool-call authorization separate from user identity, and rate/abuse controls — plus AI red-teaming that tests your systems with adversarial playbooks before attackers do.

Governance completes the program: AI asset inventory (shadow-AI discovery included), model cards with security posture, incident response runbooks for AI-specific events, and controls mapped to NIST AI RMF and ISO 42001. The output is an AI estate your CISO can defend to the board and your regulators can inspect.

The sectors where AI Security & Model Protection currently runs: Banking & Financial Services, Insurance & Risk, Healthcare & Life Sciences, Public Sector & Government. Each engagement anchors to one named metric in that sector's own language.

Shadow-AI governance
discovery, registration and policy routing of unsanctioned AI use
